primary_texts:
Richard Wilson is a third-generation farmer in California's Imperial Valley. When drought dried up his well, he stopped waiting for rain and started looking at the air.

His free video walks through what he and a friend who works on air conditioners came up with: pulling drinkable water out of humid air with the same condensation principle your AC uses.

Watch it and judge for yourself. #ad
descriptions: How condensation turns air into water
A backup water plan for dry summers

primary_texts:
Ever noticed the water dripping from your air conditioner? That's moisture pulled out of the air. On a humid day a single unit can drip gallons of it.

One drought-hit farmer asked a simple question: what if you built a machine to do that on purpose, and cleaned the water up well enough to drink?

His video shows how he went about it. #ad

Lake Mead has hit record lows in recent years. Wells across the Southwest are being drilled deeper. Towns have faced boil-water notices after storms.

Quick question: how many days of water does your home have stored right now?

Homesteaders and preppers: food storage is only half a plan. Stored water runs out, and wells run dry.

A farmer who lived through exactly that shares the DIY approach he built with a friend who repairs air conditioners: producing drinking water from the moisture in the air.

Free video for anyone serious about self-reliance. #ad

primary_texts:
"Water from thin air" sounds like a gimmick. The principle isn't. It's condensation, the same thing that beads on a glass of iced tea and drips from your AC.

The honest catch: it works best in humid air and it runs on electricity.

The video explains how one farmer set up his own unit. Worth a look if you have ever worried about your water supply. #ad

A home unit that makes drinking water from humid air is one way people are planning for that, paired with a generator or solar for outages.
